第 1 章 Advanced PeopleOps—One-on-One Retrospectives高级 PeopleOps——一对一会议复盘

Marcus Blankenship / 马库斯·布兰肯希普

— 第 13 页 —

Carmen's heart sunk as she looked at her calendar. Back-to-back one-on-one meetings filled her day, overflowing into the next.

卡门看着日历，心沉了下去。连续不断的一对一会议排满了她一整天，甚至还要溢出到第二天。

"Ugh…maybe I could call in sick. Or make up an excuse to work from home. My boss wouldn't care. My team would be thrilled to skip them."

「唉……要不我装病请假吧。或者编个理由在家办公。我老板才不会在乎呢。我的团队要是能跳过这些会议，估计都要乐疯了。」

"It's not too late, you can still call in sick," she thought as she stood in the Starbucks line, "But then what kind of boss would you be? It sucks, and everyone hates it, but you have to do it."

「现在还不晚，你还能装病请假，」她站在星巴克排队时想着，「但那样你算什么老板呢？这玩意儿确实烂透了，谁都讨厌，但你就是得做。」

"Sheesh, what are we gonna talk about? I guess I'll just ask people what they're working on this week, and hopefully, I can get each one done in five minutes. Oh! Or maybe we could do them in small groups! That would take soooooo much less time."

「天呐，我们到底聊啥呢？要不就问问大家这周在做什么吧，希望每个人五分钟就能搞定。哦！要不咱们搞小组会议吧！那样能省超多时间！」

"I'd better order an extra-large coffee with quad shots…I'm going to need it."

「我最好点杯超大杯、四份浓缩的咖啡……今天得靠它撑着了。」

Apply What You Already Know运用你已有的经验

I'm going to share a head-smackingly simple lesson that has served me well. Ready?

我要分享一个超级简单的教训——简单到你拍脑袋都能想到——但它让我受益匪浅。准备好了吗？

Make every fourth one-on-one meeting a retrospective to discuss improvements to your one-on-ones.

把每第四次一对一会议变成一次复盘会，专门讨论怎么改进你们的一对一。

This is similar to a sprint retrospective, and you can use the same format. The point of a sprint retrospective is for the team to improve. The point of this retrospective is to improve your one-on-ones, making them more valuable for both of you.

这和 Sprint 复盘很像，你可以用同样的形式。Sprint 复盘的目的是让团队变得更好；而这个复盘的目的是让你的一对一变得更好，让它对你们双方都更有价值。

— 第 14 页 —

That's it. Go do it.

就这么简单。去做吧。

But, if you need a nudge…

不过，如果你需要推一把的话……

Here are five steps to help you start:

这里有五个步骤帮你开始：

  1. Let each team member know that the next one-on-one meeting will be used to discuss your one-on-one meetings.提前告诉每位团队成员：下一次一对一会议将专门用来讨论你们的一对一会议本身。
  2. Ask them to write down what's working for them, what's not working, and ideas for change. You will do the same.让他们写下：哪些方面效果不错、哪些不太行、以及可以改进的想法。你自己也一样做。
  3. During the meeting, discuss what you both wrote, just like in a normal retrospective.会议上，像普通复盘那样讨论你们各自写的内容。
  4. Brainstorm a list together of possible actions that will improve the meetings.一起头脑风暴，列出可以改善会议的行动项。
  5. Choose a few actions, again together, to try for the next three meetings, and then discuss them in your next one-on-one retrospective.再一起挑出几项行动，在接下来的三次会议中试行，然后在下一次一对一复盘时回顾效果。

Simply start talking about your one-on-ones with the other person and discuss how they could be better.

就是这么简单——开始和对方聊聊你们的一对一，讨论怎么才能让它变得更好。

What If You're Not the Boss?如果你不是老板怎么办？

What can you do to improve a one-on-one that is inflicted on you? Here are some simple, but maybe not easy, ways to broach the subject with your boss:

如果一对一是被强加给你的，你能做些什么来改善它？这里有一些简单——但可能并不容易——的方法，可以用来跟老板开口谈这件事：

  • Forward this article to your boss, with a note that you'd like to try one-on-one retrospectives.把这篇文章转发给你的老板，附一句话说你想试试一对一复盘。
  • In your next one-on-one meeting, ask if you can take a few minutes to discuss how the meeting can be improved.在下一次一对一会议上，问能不能花几分钟讨论一下怎么改进会议本身。
  • Brainstorm a retro-style "glad-sad-mad" list about the meeting and bring it to the next meeting.用复盘式的「开心-难过-生气」清单来梳理这个会议，然后带到下次会议上。
  • Ask your boss what the real goal of the meeting is and whether they feel this format is working.问问老板这个会议的真正目的是什么，以及他们觉得目前的形式有没有效果。
  • Let your boss know that the current meeting format frustrates you and that you'd like to discuss changing it.让老板知道目前的会议形式让你很沮丧，你想讨论一下怎么改变。
  • Tell your boss the way you feel about your one-on-one meetings, and then ask how they feel about them.告诉老板你对一对一会议的感受，然后问问他们的感受如何。

Talk about what's really happening. Stop pretending that your one-on-ones are great, or that they can't be changed, or that you're benefiting from them as much as you could be.

聊聊真正发生了什么。别再假装你的一对一很棒、或者假装它无法改变、又或者假装你已经从中获得了全部价值。

Best case: the meetings will improve, your boss will appreciate your initiative, and you'll do better work.

最好的情况：会议变得更好了，老板欣赏你的主动性，你的工作也做得更出色。

— 第 15 页 —

Worst case: your boss says, "No, things are fine as is. How dare you suggest they could be improved? Just give me your status update."

最坏的情况：你的老板说，「不，现在这样就挺好。你怎么敢说它还能改进？直接跟我汇报进度就行了。」

(If the worst case happens, you have bigger problems than crummy one-on-one meetings.)

（如果最坏情况真的发生了，那你面临的问题可比糟糕的一对一会议严重多了。）

What Kinds of Things Can Be Changed About a 1:1 Meeting?一对一会议里有哪些东西可以改变？

It's easy to fall into a rut with your one-on-one meetings, like an old married couple can fall into a pattern about how they spend Friday nights. Here are 10 things about your one-on-ones that you could change but might not have considered. (There are surely many more, but this should get your creative juices flowing.)

一对一会议很容易陷入套路，就像一对老夫妻每周五晚上都按同一个模式过一样。这里有 10 件关于一对一的事情，你可以改变但可能从没想过。（当然肯定还有更多，但这些应该能让你脑洞大开了。）

  • How often you meet (it doesn't have to be the same frequency with each person)见面频率（不必每个人都用同样的频率）
  • What time you meet (it doesn't have to always be at the same time)见面时间（不必每次都固定在同一时间）
  • Who runs the meeting (how could you take turns running the meeting?)谁来主持会议（你们可以怎么轮流主持？）
  • Where you meet (consider a walking meeting or a breakfast meeting)在哪里见面（试试边走边聊的会议，或者早餐会议）
  • What preparation both of you do for the meeting (try more, or less, prep)双方会前做多少准备（试试多准备一点，或者少准备一点）
  • The agenda for the meeting会议议程
  • The goal of the meeting会议目标
  • The length of the meeting会议时长
  • The communication medium (face-to-face, telephone, Slack, Skype, etc.)沟通媒介（面对面、电话、Slack、Skype 等）
  • What you could combine it with (a meal, a walk, a commute, etc.)可以和什么事结合起来（吃饭、散步、通勤等）

Do You Wait Too Long to Consider a Change?你是不是等了太久才想着改变？

When I begin to feel in a rut, I ask myself some questions. In particular, I ask whether my current practices still fit with my current situation or reality. Often, I find that this one question allows me to be more agile, more creative, and less judging. It lets me see new possibilities that I'd been missing.

当我开始觉得陷入套路时，我会问自己一些问题。特别是，我会问自己：目前的做法还适应当前的情况和现实吗？我发现，光是这一个问题就能让我变得更灵活、更有创造力、更少评判。它让我看到之前一直忽略的新可能性。

For example, if I were dreading my one-on-ones, I might ask questions such as these:

举个例子，如果我开始害怕一对一会议了，我可能会问这样一些问题：

  • What is my secret goal for these meetings?我对这些会议的隐秘目标是什么？
  • What is my spoken goal for them?我嘴上说的目标是什么？
  • What is the other person's goal for them?对方的目标是什么？
— 第 16 页 —
  • What is the company's goal for them?公司对这些会议的目标是什么？
  • What would happen if we stopped doing them?如果我们不开这些会议了会怎样？
  • What parts are valuable to me and which feel like a waste?哪些部分对我有价值，哪些感觉是浪费时间？
  • What parts are valuable to them and which feel like a waste?哪些部分对对方有价值，哪些感觉是浪费时间？
  • What is the least we could do and still have a valuable one-on-one meeting?我们最少做到什么程度，还能让一对一有价值？
  • What do we need to add, subtract, change?我们需要增加什么、减少什么、改变什么？

Grandma's Ham奶奶的火腿

Albert Einstein summed it up pretty well when he said, "The important thing is not to stop questioning."

爱因斯坦有句话总结得特别好：「重要的是不要停止提问。」

Jane asked her mother, "Why do you cut the ends off the ham before baking it?"

简问她妈妈：「为什么烤火腿之前要把两头切掉？」

Her mother answered, "Because that's how your grandma taught me to do it. Ask Grandma."

她妈妈回答：「因为你奶奶就是这么教我的。去问奶奶吧。」

When Jane asked her Grandma, she replied, "My roasting pan was small, so I had to cut the ends off the ham to fit it in the pan."

简去问奶奶，奶奶回答：「我的烤盘太小了，所以得把火腿两头切掉才能放进锅里。」

It's difficult to question the status quo.

质疑现状是很难的。

Not just because you want to avoid looking dumb or rocking the boat or breaking tradition, but because you might not realize there's a question to ask.

不只是因为你不想显得傻、不想惹麻烦、不想打破传统，还因为你可能根本意识不到这里有个问题可以问。

New possibilities are wonderful. New choices and options do exist about how we work together. New possibilities bring hope that the future doesn't need to be like the past and that we can grow and improve.

新的可能性是美好的。关于我们如何协作，确实存在新的选择和方案。新的可能性带来希望——未来不必和过去一样，我们可以成长、可以进步。

What a great thought!

这是多棒的想法啊！
